title: Deadline Is Now
tagline: A tip that could be the story of the year, twenty minutes to verify it, and an editor who wants it filed by six.

wake_up.text: Your phone has eleven notifications before you're fully awake — the overnight news desk, a source, and an editor already asking where yesterday's follow-up piece is.

choices.text: Read through everything before responding to anyone
Skim for what's actually urgent and move

morning_pitch.text: Morning editorial meeting. You pitch today's follow-up piece; the editor wants it filed with real depth, not a rehash.

choices.text: Commit to a real deep-dive version, even if it takes longer
Pitch a safer, faster version instead

random_moment.text: The newsroom fills in around you the way it always does mid-morning — a little differently every day.

choices.text: A colleague passes along a useful lead unprompted
The printer jams at the worst possible moment
Someone does a coffee run for the whole desk

source_call.text: A source calls back with the detail you needed for the follow-up — reluctant, but it's on the record if you handle it carefully.

choices.text: Take the extra time to protect their identity properly
Get the quote and move fast toward deadline

midday_deadline.text: The follow-up piece is filed. Your editor is already asking what's next — and what's next just landed in your inbox.

choices.text: Open the new message

breaking_tip.text: An anonymous tip lands: a local official is allegedly involved in something serious. If it's true, it's the biggest story of the year. If it's wrong, it's a career-damaging retraction. You have maybe twenty minutes before a rival outlet could have the same tip.

choices.text: Verify with your one strong source and publish fast
Hold it and seek a second independent source first
Call the official's office directly for comment before running anything
Publish based on the tip alone, sourced anonymously

tip_outcome_fast.text: The story goes up first, ahead of anyone else, and it holds up under the scrutiny that follows. Fast and right — this time.

choices.text: Handle the aftermath

tip_outcome_careful.text: The second source takes twenty extra minutes to reach — and confirms everything, with a detail the first source never mentioned. The story that runs is airtight.

choices.text: Handle the aftermath

tip_outcome_comment.text: The official's office denies everything on the record — which becomes its own part of the story, and protects you from a one-sided piece if this ever gets contested.

choices.text: Handle the aftermath

tip_outcome_anonymous.text: The story runs fast and gets attention fast — and by evening, the details are already unraveling under public scrutiny. This is exactly the kind of story that follows a reporter around.

choices.text: Handle the aftermath

afternoon_followup.text: Reaction to the story is already rolling in — some of it useful, some of it just noise. Your editor wants a same-day follow-up.

choices.text: Engage thoughtfully with the substantive criticism
Ignore the noise and move straight to the next piece

evening_filing.text: One more piece due before the desk closes for the night — the corrections/clarifications process if anything in today's stories needs it.

choices.text: Review every fact in today's pieces one more time
Trust the work already done and call it a day

end_shift.text: The newsroom quiets down for the night. Tomorrow's front page is already half-decided by what happened today.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Front Page, Airtight
triumphant.blurb: The story of the year, verified and unshakeable. This is the byline people remember.

steady_hand.title: Solid Reporting
steady_hand.blurb: No corrections, no controversy — just careful, accurate journalism all day long.

ordinary_day.title: Another Deadline Made
ordinary_day.blurb: A full news day, filed and closed. Tomorrow's deadline is already ticking.

burned_out.title: Running on Fumes
burned_out.blurb: You filed everything, but you're not sure how. Deadline after deadline, this pace has a real cost.

written_up.title: Correction Pending
written_up.blurb: Something in today's reporting is going to need a formal correction. The story ran. The facts are still being sorted out.
